Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Reports in Indian ocean
Expected_Answer: Mandatory and voluntary ship reporting systems including: 1. INDSAR (Indian Search and Rescue system maintained by Indian Coast Guard), 2. INSPIRES (Indian Ship Reporting System for naval tracking), 3. Straits Ship Report (STRAITREP) in Malacca, and 4. Amver (global voluntary reporting).
Reg_Source: SOLAS Ch. V Reg 11 / Indian Merchant Shipping Rules
Fail_Trigger: Failing to know INDSAR or INSPIRES boundaries when navigating within the Indian Ocean region.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Nav area in India
Expected_Answer: India administers NAVAREA VIII (8). It extends from the East Coast of Africa across the Indian Ocean down to 30°S and east towards the Indonesian archipelago. The National Coordinator is the Chief Hydrographer to the Government of India.
Fail_Trigger: Stating that India belongs to NAVAREA III or failing to identify that the Indian Naval Hydrographic Office issues NAVAREA VIII warnings.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Outbound you see preferred channel to stbd buoy right ahead
Expected_Answer: IALA Region A Buoyage. A modified lateral buoy (Red with a green horizontal band). It indicates that the primary/preferred channel is to the PORT side of the buoy (i.e., you leave the buoy on your starboard side as an outbound vessel).
Fail_Trigger: Steering to the starboard side of the buoy, which places the ship into the secondary channel or shallow water.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: How will you guide 2nd officer in passage planning
Expected_Answer: Enforce the 4 stages: Appraisal, Planning, Execution, and Monitoring. Instruct him to consult charts, hydrographic data, routing guides, UKC policies, and weather limitations. The plan must be executed berth-to-berth and signed by all watchkeeping officers before departure.
Reg_Source: SOLAS Ch. V Reg 34 / IMO Res A.893(21)
Fail_Trigger: Allowing a passage plan to be compiled without checking dynamic UKC margins or failing to get all watchkeepers to physically sign it.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: One vessel overtaking you and ROC exists what action will you take
Expected_Answer: Under Rule 13, the overtaking vessel must keep completely out of the way of the overtaken vessel. As the overtaken vessel, maintain course and speed (Rule 17). If the give-way vessel takes no action, take action to avoid collision by your maneuver alone, signaling your intentions.
Fail_Trigger: Altering course blindly to port into the path of the overtaking vessel or failing to sound the 5 short and rapid blasts warning signal.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: LLMC (Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims)
Expected_Answer: An international convention allowing shipowners and salvors to limit their financial liability for maritime claims (such as loss of life, personal injury, or property damage) based on a sliding scale linked to the ship's gross tonnage.
Fail_Trigger: Failing to state that liability limits are calculated strictly based on ship tonnage (GT) using Special Drawing Rights (SDRs).

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: LOF and SCOPIC difference
Expected_Answer: LOF (Lloyd's Open Form) operates on the traditional "No Cure, No Pay" concept (Article 12). SCOPIC (Special Compensation P&I Club Clause) is an optional clause rolled into LOF that provides a tariff-based payment to cover salvor expenses + profit if there is a threat to the environment, regardless of "cure".
Fail_Trigger: Stating that a salvor receives zero compensation under SCOPIC if the ship breaks up and sinks completely.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Salvage and Towing difference
Expected_Answer: Salvage: An unscheduled, urgent operation executed to save a vessel from real maritime peril; rewards are governed by maritime law and are high. Towing: A pre-arranged commercial contract to accelerate or assist a vessel's normal transit; paid via fixed commercial tariffs without any "peril" requirement.
Fail_Trigger: Claiming salvage awards for a routine, non-emergency harbour towage operation.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Scopic and article 14 difference
Expected_Answer: Article 14 (Special Compensation) requires the salvor to prove a distinct threat to the environment and relies on slow, highly litigated tribunal assessments. SCOPIC replaces Article 14 litigations with an immediate, pre-agreed daily tariff payment backed by a security deposit from the P&I club within 2 working days.
Reg_Source: International Salvage Convention 1989 Art. 14 / SCOPIC Clause
Fail_Trigger: Failing to point out that SCOPIC eliminates the legal requirement to prove an environmental threat to obtain expenses.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: 4 salient features of Salvage
Expected_Answer: 1. Existence of a real maritime danger/peril. 2. Service must be voluntary (not bound by prior official duty). 3. The operation must achieve a useful result/success ("No Cure, No Pay" baseline). 4. A maritime lien is automatically created against the salved property.
Fail_Trigger: Claiming a salvage reward for services rendered when the vessel was completely safe and out of any tangible peril.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: How to dock a vessel with bow damage
Expected_Answer: Assess internal structural integrity and boundary bulkheads. Trim the vessel by the stern to raise the damaged bow area above the water level. Ensure the dry dock operator alters the block arrangement (keel blocks) to support the deformed bow structure without crushing it. Ballast/deballast symmetrically to avoid racking.
Reg_Source: Shipyard Drydocking Manual / SOLAS Ch. II-1
Fail_Trigger: Attempting to dock with the damaged bow flooded, causing massive localized load concentration and structural collapse on the forward blocks.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Gen Avg security
Expected_Answer: Before cargo is released at destination following a General Average declaration, the cargo owner must provide GA Security: 1. A signed General Average Bond (Lloyd's Average Bond), and 2. A GA Guarantee from the cargo underwriters or a cash deposit.
Fail_Trigger: Releasing commercial cargo to a receiver before securing the signed General Average Bond and underwriter guarantee.

Question: what guidance will provide to 2/O if passage from Japan to Vancouver
Expected_Answer: Mandate a Great Circle (GC) track to minimize distance, but implement rhumb-line segments to avoid extreme high latitudes during winter storms. Enforce compliance with the North Pacific Voluntary Tanker Routing Agreement, check load line zones (Winter/Summer), update Aleutian Islands weather tracking, and integrate cold-weather checklists (fuel heating, deck de-icing).
Reg_Source: SOLAS Ch. V Reg 34 / IMO Res A.893(21)
Fail_Trigger: Allowing the 2/O to plot a rigid Great Circle route that enters dangerous sub-polar freezing zones or violating seasonal load line boundaries.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: Rule 2
Expected_Answer: Rule 2 establishes that rules cannot substitute for good seamanship. It allows or mandates a departure from the strict text of the rules if necessary to avoid immediate maritime danger, accounting for all special circumstances including vessel limitations.
Fail_Trigger: Arguing that you must strictly maintain course and speed as a stand-on vessel even when a collision becomes unavoidable by the give-way vessel's action alone.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: In RV when can you alter to port
Expected_Answer: Under Rule 19(d)(i), an alteration of course to port for a vessel forward of the beam is strictly prohibited if that vessel is another vessel detected by radar alone. You can only alter to port if the target is being overtaken (astern or well abaft the beam).
Fail_Trigger: Altering course to port for a vessel detected on your port or starboard bow in restricted visibility (an immediate critical fail).

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: On vessel right ahead, 1 port bow, 1 stbd bow action and as per which rule
Expected_Answer: In sight of one another: Rule 14 (Head-on) applies to the vessel right ahead (both alter to starboard). Rule 15 (Crossing) applies to the vessel on your starboard bow (you are give-way, alter to starboard/pass astern). You are stand-on (Rule 17) for the vessel on your port bow. Perform a bold, early alteration to starboard to clear the right-ahead and starboard targets simultaneously.
Fail_Trigger: Altering course to port in a multiple-vessel crossing/head-on trap, crossing ahead of the starboard bow vessel.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: Cards: Single white light And cross questions
Expected_Answer: Could indicate: 1. A vessel under 7 meters, 2. A vessel seen from right astern (stern light), 3. An anchor light for a vessel under 50m. *Cross question reflex*: Treat as a power-driven vessel being overtaken (Rule 13). Maintain course and speed but monitor closely; if aspect changes to reveal sidelights, reassess crossing rules.
Fail_Trigger: Assuming a single white light is static or always a vessel at anchor without preparing for an overtaking or close-quarters evaluation.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: Shipper dec as per which section of IMSBC
Expected_Answer: Section 4 of the IMSBC Code (Assessment of acceptability of consignments for safe shipment). The shipper must provide the Master with valid, written cargo information and declarations well in advance of loading.
Reg_Source: IMSBC Code Section 4 / SOLAS Ch. VI Reg 2
Fail_Trigger: Accepting a solid bulk cargo consignment without a signed, written Shipper's Declaration form confirming cargo group status.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: draft survey full detail and purpose
Expected_Answer: A highly precise displacement calculation method using forward, aft, and midship drafts (port/starboard) corrected for water density, hog/sag, trim (1st/2nd corrections), and list. *Purpose*: Commercially quantifies the exact weight of cargo loaded or discharged by accounting for total ballast, fuel, and constants.
Fail_Trigger: Neglecting to read density at the draft marks or omitting the second trim correction (layer correction) for high trim angles.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: Grain qty to be loaded how to calculate
Expected_Answer: Calculate maximum available lifting capacity (Deadweight minus fuel, water, stores, constants). Check maximum volumetric capacity of holds. Apply the International Grain Code stability criteria: calculate the volumetric heeling moments, verify that total cargo weight ensures residual GM >= 0.30m, and ensure the angle of heel due to grain shift is <= 12 degrees.
Reg_Source: International Grain Code / SOLAS Ch. VI
Fail_Trigger: Exceeding the allowable volumetric heeling moment limits, resulting in a non-compliant, unsafe departure grain stability condition.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: Class 7 loading req
Expected_Answer: Class 7 (Radioactive materials). Requires: 1. Strict segregation from crew accommodation, working areas, and undeveloped photographic films based on transport index (TI), 2. Verification of the Special Stowage Category, 3. Specialized emergency monitoring instruments, 4. Port state and transit state prior-authorization documentation.
Reg_Source: IMDG Code Class 7 / SOLAS Ch. VII
Fail_Trigger: Stowing Class 7 packages adjacent to the bridge or crew living quarters, causing high-dose radiation exposure risk.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: Cargo docs for GAS
Expected_Answer: 1. Certificate of Fitness for the Carriage of Liquefied Gases in Bulk. 2. Cargo Manifest and Dangerous Goods Declaration. 3. Certificate of Cargo Quality and Origin. 4. Bill of Lading. 5. Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS). 6. Tank Pre-cargo preparation/Inerting records.
Reg_Source: IGC Code / SOLAS Ch. VII Part C
Fail_Trigger: Loading a liquefied gas cargo without verifying that the specific gas chemical name is listed on the ship's Certificate of Fitness.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: Function of B/L
Expected_Answer: 1. Evidence of the Contract of Carriage. 2. Receipt for Cargo loaded on board (stating quantity/condition). 3. Document of Title (enables ownership transfer of the goods).
Reg_Source: Hague-Visby Rules / Indian Bills of Lading Act
Fail_Trigger: Stating that a Bill of Lading *is* the actual contract of carriage itself, rather than acting as *evidence* of it.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: Ms Circ reg iron ore fines/ concentrate loading
Expected_Answer: DG Shipping MS Notice 10 of 2011 (and relevant MS Circular updates) mandates strict sampling, testing, and loading protocols for iron ore fines. Requires independent laboratory verification of TML and actual moisture content (MC) taken within 7 days of loading. The Master must carry out a "Can Test" onboard if moisture ingress is suspected.
Reg_Source: DG Shipping MS Notice 10 of 2011 / IMSBC Code
Fail_Trigger: Accepting an iron ore fines consignment where the shipper's moisture sample date exceeds 7 days prior to the loading date.

Surveyor_Name: Int: Capt. R. Sikarwar / Ext: Capt. P. Kumar
Question: No B/L at discharge port Action
Expected_Answer: The Master must strictly refuse to discharge or release the cargo. If the commercial charterer demands release, the Master may release cargo *only* upon receipt of a valid, original Letter of Indemnity (LOI) counter-signed by a first-class international bank, explicitly approved by the shipowner and P&I Club.
Fail_Trigger: Discharging cargo to a local receiver without either the original Bill of Lading or a verified, Owner/P&I-approved bank-backed LOI.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Why min trim by astern
Expected_Answer: 1. Ensures 100% efficient drainage/stripping of aft ballast/cargo suction wells. 2. Guarantees maximum propeller immersion for efficient propulsion thrust. 3. Enhances directional rudder control and course-keeping stability. 4. Prevents bow pounding or slamming damage in head seas.
Reg_Source: Ship Stability & Trim Principles / SOLAS Ch. II-1

Expected_Answer: The Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (repealing the 1958 Act) reorganizes Indian maritime law into a streamlined 16 Parts / 325 Clauses. Key changes: Replaces DGS with the Director-General of Marine Administration (DGMA), expands vessel definition to submersibles/drones, allows OCI/LLP ship ownership, implements digital electronic registration, and enforces strict statutory pollution compliance for all vessels.
Fail_Trigger: Quoting the outdated 561-section framework of the 1958 Act or failing to recognize the active transition to the DGMA framework.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Anchor PMS
Expected_Answer: Planned Maintenance System for ground tackle includes: 1. Quarterly inspection of windlass brake linings, hydraulic pressures, and secure pins. 2. Semi-annual inspection of chain locker drainage and bitter end release device. 3. Dry dock ranging of cable to measure mean diameter wear (maximum allowable reduction is 12% before condemning).
Reg_Source: SOLAS Ch. II-1 Reg 45 / Class Rules
Fail_Trigger: Failing to verify the mechanical functionality of the bitter end quick-release device during scheduled safety inspections.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: C/O duty as per ISM
Expected_Answer: As the Management-Level Operations Officer under the ISM framework, the Chief Officer must: 1. Maintain the ship's safety administration and update the Safety Management System (SMS) records. 2. Act as the Shipboard Safety Officer, executing risk assessments, toolbox meets, and investigating near-misses. 3. Enforce environmental management policies (garbage, oily water). 4. Report all non-conformities directly to the Master/DPA.
Reg_Source: ISM Code Section 5 & 7 / SOLAS Ch. IX
Fail_Trigger: Failing to take active ownership of risk assessments or claiming that SMS records are strictly the Master's individual responsibility.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Martin / Int: Capt. G.P. Shenoy
Question: Running Moor
Expected_Answer: An anchoring maneuver used in confined waters with a strong, reversing tidal stream to limit swinging room. Drop the first anchor (riding anchor) while heading *with* the current, pay out double the required cable scope, drop the second anchor (lee anchor) after snubbing, and heave back on the first cable until the vessel rides midway between both anchors.
Fail_Trigger: Dropping the second anchor prematurely before the vessel has gathered sufficient sternway, causing the chains to entangle and foul the windlass.

Strikingly beautiful or unusual crimson sunsets.

Drop the second anchor (lee anchor). 5. Heave in the first cable while paying out the second cable until the vessel sits exactly midway between both anchors with an equal scope (e.g., 4-5 shackles each).

DGPS (Differential GPS) enhances this by using a network of fixed, surveyed ground-based reference stations. These stations calculate atmospheric/orbital timing errors and broadcast real-time correction factors to the ship via VHF/MF. DGPS accuracy is significantly superior, narrowing the positional error down to less than 1 to 3 meters.
Reg_Source: IMO Res A.1046(27) / SOLAS Ch. V
Fail_Trigger: Stating that standard GPS is more accurate than DGPS, or failing to identify that ground stations provide the error corrections.

Question: CBD crossing situations
Expected_Answer: A Vessel Constrained by her Draft (CBD) exhibits 3 vertical Red lights / a Black cylinder. In sight of one another, a CBD vessel does *not* have a blanket right-of-way over crossing power-driven vessels. Under Rule 18, a standard PDV shall, *if the circumstances of the case admit*, avoid impeding the safe passage of a CBD vessel. However, if a close-quarters situation develops and risk of collision exists, standard crossing rules (Rule 15) apply. Question: What is trs at what latitude it is formed
Expected_Answer: A Tropical Revolving Storm (TRS) is an intense, low-pressure cyclonic storm system forming over warm tropical oceans characterized by high-speed spiraling winds (>64 knots), a calm central "Eye," and a violent "Eye Wall." It forms within a specific latitude belt, typically between **5° and 15° North and South** of the Equator, where sea surface temperatures remain consistently high (>=26.5°C).

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Ranganathan / Int: Capt. Darokar
Question: Why not near equator?
Expected_Answer: A TRS cannot form near the Equator (between 0° and 5° latitude) because the **Coriolis Force is zero at the Equator**. The Coriolis Force is the deflecting force generated by the Earth's rotation that is mathematically proportional to the sine of the latitude. Without sufficient Coriolis force to deflect moving air currents inward, the incoming air simply fills the low-pressure pocket directly, preventing the setup of a sustained, closed cyclonic rotational vortex.
Fail_Trigger: Failing to identify that a lack of Coriolis force prevents the formation of cyclonic rotation near the equator.

Question: Draft Survey and why corrections being applied
Expected_Answer: A method to calculate cargo weight loaded/discharged by analyzing changes in ship displacement. Corrections applied: 1. **Draft Mark Correction (Distance Correction):** Adjusts observed drafts to the perpendiculars because marks are rarely on the perpendicular lines. 2. **Hog/Sag Correction (Mean of Means):** Compensates for hull longitudinal deflection/bending. 3. **First Trim Correction:** Adjusts for the longitudinal shift of the center of flotation (CF) away from midships. 4. **Second Trim Correction (Layer Correction):** Accounts for the change in TPC value over a large trim angle as the waterplane area shifts shape. 5. **Density Correction:** Corrects calculated displacement from dock water density to standard sea water/fresh water scales.
Reg_Source: UN ECE Draft Survey Standards / Ship Stability Manual
Fail_Trigger: Omitting the Second Trim Correction at high trim angles, or failing to measure the true dock water density at the exact depth of the draft marks.

Question: How to make Gyro North Seeking
Expected_Answer: A free gyroscope is made north-seeking by introducing a control force that counteracts the Earth's rotation (apparent drift and tilt). This is achieved by fitting a **bottom-heavy liquid ballistic system (mercury/oil ballistic)** or a **top-heavy gravity weight configuration**. When the gyro axle tilts due to Earth's rotation, gravity applies a downward force. This creates a precessional torque at right angles to the force, causing the gyro axle to precess horizontally back towards the true geographical meridian.

For a target abeam or abaft the beam, avoid altering course toward it. If a fog signal is heard forward of the beam, reduce speed to minimum steerage way or stop, and navigate with extreme caution until danger is past.
Fail_Trigger: Using visual terminology like "stand-on" or altering course to port for a target forward of the beam detected on radar alone.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: CBD crossing situations
Expected_Answer: A Vessel Constrained by her Draft (CBD) exhibits 3 vertical Red lights / a Black cylinder. In sight of one another, a CBD vessel does *not* have a blanket right-of-way over crossing power-driven vessels. Under Rule 18, a standard PDV shall, *if the circumstances of the case admit*, avoid impeding the safe passage of a CBD vessel. However, if a close-quarters situation develops and risk of collision exists, standard crossing rules (Rule 15) apply. If the CBD is on your starboard bow, you are the give-way vessel; execute an early turn to starboard to pass astern. If she is on your port bow, she must still follow the rules, but you must sound the doubt signal if she fails to act.
Fail_Trigger: Claiming that a CBD vessel has an absolute, blanket right-of-way that completely voids standard crossing rule obligations.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: SHA definition
Expected_Answer: Sidereal Hour Angle. The angular distance measured westward along the celestial equator from the First Point of Aries to the hour circle of a celestial body, ranging from 0 degrees to 360 degrees. It remains relatively constant for stars over long periods, allowing efficient celestial sight reductions.
Fail_Trigger: Defining SHA as an eastward measurement or confusing it with Greenwich Hour Angle (GHA).

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: First point of Aries definitely (he wants as per book)
Expected_Answer: The exact point on the celestial sphere where the Sun crosses the celestial equator from South to North during the vernal equinox. It serves as the datum point or astronomical origin (000° longitude) on the celestial sphere from which the Sidereal Hour Angles (SHA) of all stars are measured westward.
Fail_Trigger: Providing a vague definition without specifying the Sun crossing the celestial equator from South to North during the vernal equinox.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: TLD
Expected_Answer: Tropical Low Depression. A cyclonic storm formation phase characterized by a distinct, closed cyclonic wind circulation pattern with sustained wind speeds of less than 34 knots surrounding a low-pressure core. It represents the preliminary stage of a Tropical Revolving Storm (TRS).
Fail_Trigger: Stating that a TLD contains hurricane-force winds or failing to recognize it as the preliminary stage of a TRS.

Question: Angle of Repose
Expected_Answer: The maximum slope angle (measured from the horizontal plane) at which a non-cohesive granular bulk material will remain stable without sliding. Bulk cargoes with an angle of repose <= 35 degrees are highly fluid and prone to shifting, requiring extensive trimming under international codes.
Fail_Trigger: Failing to note that a low angle of repose increases the immediate risk of cargo shift, or confusing it with the angle of loll.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Hazards of Concentrates and Coal
Expected_Answer: Concentrates: Liquefaction risk (Group A) where compaction and moisture create a fluid slurry, completely destroying shear strength and creating a massive free surface effect. Coal: Self-heating, spontaneous combustion, emits explosive Methane (CH4) and highly toxic Carbon Monoxide (CO), and creates a highly corrosive acid environment when wet.
Reg_Source: IMSBC Code schedules for COAL / Concentrates
Fail_Trigger: Executing continuous under-deck through-ventilation on a self-heating coal cargo, which injects oxygen into the hold and triggers an explosion.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: All about Isgott

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Imdg, contents
Expected_Answer: The International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code regulates the safe carriage of packaged dangerous goods. Volume 1: General provisions, definitions, training, packaging/tank specs, and operational consignment procedures. Volume 2: The Dangerous Goods List (DGL Columns 1 to 18 detailing UN Numbers, classes, labels, special provisions), and Limited Quantities exceptions. Supplement: Contains EmS Guide, MFAG, BC Code, and Infested Cargo provisions.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: X,Y, Z categories of cargo
Expected_Answer: MARPOL Annex II pollution categories for Noxious Liquid Substances (NLS) in bulk: Category X: Major hazard to marine resources/human health; discharge strictly prohibited, mandates an immediate port pre-wash. Category Y: Deemed a hazard; limits operational discharge quantities. Category Z: Minor hazard; imposes less stringent discharge criteria. Other Substances (OS): Non-hazardous.
Fail_Trigger: Failing to state that Category X chemicals pose the highest environmental threat and mandate a mandatory port pre-wash.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: What is BL, types of BL (17 types background)
Expected_Answer: A legally binding commercial document serving three functions: 1. Conclusive receipt for cargo description, weight, and condition. 2. Prima facie evidence of the contract of carriage. 3. Document of Title. Key types include: Straight, Order, Bearer, Clean, Claused/Dirty, Shipped on Board, Received for Shipment, Switch, Through, Combined Transport, Sea Waybill, and Charter Party B/L.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Mates receipt

It acts as prima facie evidence of receipt, which the shipper later exchanges for the final Bill of Lading.
Fail_Trigger: Signing a clean Mate's Receipt for a cargo parcel showing visible discoloration or loading temperature deviations at the manifold.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Annex 2 discharge criteria
Expected_Answer: For permitted NLS residues (Categories Y or Z): 1. Vessel must be en route at a speed >= 7 knots (4 knots for barges). 2. Discharge must be below the waterline via the dedicated underwater discharge outlet. 3. Must be executed at a distance >= 12 nautical miles from the nearest land. 4. Water depth must be >= 25 meters. Category X residues require a mandatory port pre-wash first.
Fail_Trigger: Proposing to discharge any Annex II chemical residue while the vessel is stationary or drifting, or executing a discharge above the waterline.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Pre wash Requirements
Expected_Answer: Mandatory for all Category X cargo tanks, high-viscosity or solidifying Category Y substances, or when a tank is not cleared to stripping limits. Requirements: Must be executed at the discharge port before the vessel sails, using parameters (temperature, pressure, duration) specified in the P&A manual. Wash water effluent must be pumped directly to shore reception facilities until the tank is officially certified clear by a surveyor.
Reg_Source: MARPOL Annex II Regulation 13 / IBC Code
Fail_Trigger: Sailing from a discharge port with raw Category X residues onboard without executing a mandatory, surveyor-certified port pre-wash.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: RO and class difference
Expected_Answer: Classification Society: A private technical organization that establishes and enforces its own structural, mechanical, and electrical rules for building and maintaining ships. Recognized Organization (RO): A Classification Society that has been formally delegated sovereign executive authority by a Flag State Administration to conduct statutory surveys and issue statutory international certificates (e.g., SOLAS, MARPOL, Loadline) on behalf of that government.
Reg_Source: IMO RO Code (Res MSC.349(92)) / SOLAS Ch. XI-1 Reg 1
Fail_Trigger: Claiming that a Classification Society has the automatic right to issue international statutory certificates without a formal Flag State delegation agreement.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Pyrotechnics on bridge
Expected_Answer: The navigation bridge must be equipped with a water-resistant container housing a minimum of 12 Rocket Parachute Flares. Additionally, the bridge wings house 2 Lifebuoys fitted with self-igniting lights and mandatory self-activating smoke signals (Quick Release/Man Overboard markers). All pyrotechnics must be inspected monthly, kept dry, and replaced before their explicit stamped expiration date (typically 3 years from manufacture).
Reg_Source: SOLAS Chapter III Regulation 6 / LSA Code Ch. III
Fail_Trigger: Carrying less than 12 rocket parachute flares on the bridge or failing to manifest expired pyrotechnics as hazardous waste.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Rocket parachute info
Expected_Answer: Technical specifications under the LSA Code: 1. Must be contained in a water-resistant casing. 2. Must feature integral, clear ignition instructions. 3. When fired vertically, it must reach a minimum altitude of 300 meters. 4. At or near the top of its trajectory, it must eject a parachute flare that burns with a bright cherry-red color with a minimum luminous intensity of 30,000 candelas for a burning period of not less than 40 seconds. 5. Descent speed must not exceed 5 meters per second and must not damage the parachute components.
Reg_Source: LSA Code Chapter III Section 3.1 / SOLAS Ch. III
Fail_Trigger: Stating an incorrect burning duration (<40 seconds), altitude (<300m), or light intensity threshold during precise cross-examination.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Parametric rolling
Expected_Answer: A highly dangerous ship-handling phenomenon causing a sudden, massive escalation in rolling angles in head or following seas. It occurs when the wave encounter period matches or equals half of the ship's natural rolling period. This causes the waterplane area and initial stability (GM) to fluctuate drastically as wave crests and troughs pass the midship section. Prevention/Avoidance: Immediately execute a bold alteration of heading by 15 to 20 degrees or alter engine speed to change the wave encounter frequency and break the resonant synchronization.
Reg_Source: Bridge Procedures Guide / Ship Handling Principles
Fail_Trigger: Maintaining a constant heading and speed in head seas while parametric rolling angles escalate, risking cargo shift or structural capsize.

Surveyor_Name: Ext: Capt. Menon / Int: Capt. Nitin Mukesh
Question: Certificate of Class, duties of class (with cross-examination)
Expected_Answer: Certificate of Class certifies that the ship's hull, main machinery, propulsion plants, and auxiliary systems have been surveyed and found in full structural compliance with the specific rules of that Classification Society. Duties of Class: 1. Review and approve engineering designs during ship construction. 2. Execute regular intermediate, annual, and 5-yearly special renewal hull and machinery surveys. 3. Impose 'Conditions of Class' when structural defects are noted. 4. Act as an RO to enforce international statutory maritime safety conventions.
Reg_Source: SOLAS Ch. II-1 / Class Society Rules / IACS Standards
Fail_Trigger: Asserting that Class possesses the sovereign legal power to issue a formal Port State Control detention order against a vessel.
